Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "Endress + Hauser GmbH + Co., KG"
Document: "Endress+Hauser GmbH+Co., KG"

The difference is spacing: "Endress + Hauser" vs "Endress+Hauser" and "+ Co., KG" vs "+Co., KG". This is whitespace/formatting drift around the same company name. Clearly same entity.

Which best value? The rules say for spelling drift/legal-suffix drift = same-entity. The fused record should carry... the register's canonical form is used for number/year format differences. For same-entity name drift, either could be used; but typically the register canonical form is preferred for consistency, though the document is the legal instrument. The rules explicitly say "different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)" — implying for same-entity, register's canonical form is fine. Actually the rules only specify best_value for document-noise (register) and different-entity (document) and same-entity number/year (register canonical). For same-entity name drift, reasonable to use register's canonical form for consistency. The document itself in the embedded comment says "Endress + Hauser GmbH + Co., KG" with spaces, matching the register. So register form is consistent.

Best value: "Endress + Hauser GmbH + Co., KG" (register canonical).

Verdict: same-entity. Why: only whitespace around "+" differs; same company.
